# `tfctl run start` reference

Start a new run on a workspace.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start WORKSPACE [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl run start` command creates a new plan and apply run with the most recent configuration. 

<Note>

If auto-apply is enabled on the workspace and no errors occur, the plan will be automatically applied.

</Note>

Use `--plan-only` to create a speculative plan-only run that is never applied, regardless of the workspace's auto-apply setting.

## Arguments

- `WORKSPACE` - (Required) Workspace ID or workspace name.

## Available options

The `tfctl run start` command supports the following options.

| Option | Description | Default | Required |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `--organization=NAME` | Organization name. Required when using a workspace name instead of ID. | Auto-resolved from profile or Terraform cloud config | No |
| `--debugging-mode` | Enables trace logging for this run. Sets `TF_LOG=trace` in the Terraform environment for this run. | `false` | No |
| `--message=TEXT` | A message to attach to the run. | None | No |
| `--allow-empty-apply` | Allow the run to proceed even if the plan has no changes. Useful for applying a side effect such as a Terraform upgrade when no other changes are present. | `false` | No |
| `--plan-only` | Create a speculative plan-only run that is never applied. Overrides the workspace's auto-apply setting. | `false` | No |

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Examples

### Start a new run in a workspace by ID

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123
```

### Start a new run in a workspace by name

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start my-workspace --organization my-org
```

### Start a plan-only run that will not be applied

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --plan-only
```

### Start a run with a custom message

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --message "Deploying version 2.0"
```

### Start a run with debugging enabled

```shell-session
$ tfctl run start ws-abc123 --debugging-mode
```
